card.name: Punctuation before a new list item
card.fires_on: Punctuation or a short linking word that ends a reference or field label and comes just before the next item begins. Examples are the closing bracket after a section cross-reference, the dash after a dictionary source line, and the colon after Review Date.

modes.label: Closing cross-reference
modes.description: A closing bracket or parenthesis after a [see Warnings and Precautions (5.x)] reference, before the next contraindication.

modes.label: Dictionary dash
modes.description: The dash after the dictionary edition line, right before the definition starts.

modes.label: Field label joiner
modes.description: A colon, a word like for, or a URL parameter name that sits between a label and its value.
modes.example: The median income<< for>> a household in the city was $4

card.plain: It fires on the small punctuation mark that separates a label or reference from the text that follows it.
